title: Every SAT Trap Answer, Explained
description:
SAT wrong answers aren't random. They're written to be tempting, and the same patterns show up again and again. This video covers 14 of them, 7 in Reading and Writing and 7 in Math, with an SAT-style example for each one.

Covered:
• Reading & Writing: true but irrelevant, too extreme, half right, the opposite, out of scope, "sounds right," and two choices that do the same job
• Math: answering the wrong quantity, stopping halfway, sign errors, percent and unit traps, extraneous solutions, r vs. r², and reading the wrong row or column
• A 10-second check to use before you click

All questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank.
